A finite set A in an abelian group (G,+) is dissociated if the only solution to sum_{a in A} epsilon_a * a = 0 with epsilon_a in {-1,0,1} is epsilon_a = 0 for all a. Distinct subset sums is equivalent to dissociation: if two subsets S,T have equal sums, then sum_{a in S} a - sum_{a in T} a = 0 gives a nontrivial {-1,0,1}-relation. The problem now separates into (i) an algebraic axiom (dissociation in an abelian group) and (ii) a metric/order axiom (A lies in an interval [1,N] of a totally ordered group). The bound N >> 2^n becomes a theorem about the minimum diameter of dissociated sets in (Z,+,<=). This axiomatization enables transfer: in Z/pZ the analogous quantity is the Davenport constant; in R^d the analogous question concerns lattice-free convex bodies. The Boolean cube {0,1}^n maps linearly into Z via (epsilon_1,...,epsilon_n) -> sum epsilon_i a_i, and dissociation says this map is injective. So the problem reduces to: any injection from {0,1}^n into Z with image in [0, nN] forces N >> 2^n, which is a statement about the minimal distortion of embedding the Boolean cube into a one-dimensional ordered group.

Step 1 (Structural isomorphism — Boolean cube to integers): Identify each subset S ⊆ A with its characteristic vector ε ∈ {0,1}^n. The subset-sum map σ(ε) = Σ εᵢaᵢ is a linear form on ℤ^n restricted to the Boolean cube. Distinct subset sums means σ is injective on {0,1}^n.

Step 2 (Canonical model — binary representation): When aᵢ = 2^{i−1}, σ is the binary-to-integer bijection {0,1}^n → {0,…,2^n−1}, achieving N = 2^{n−1}. This is the structural template: any A with distinct subset sums is a 'deformation' of the binary basis.

Step 3 (CRT projection): By the Chinese Remainder Theorem, injectivity of σ over ℤ implies injectivity of σ mod p for every prime p ≤ max range. Since {0,1}^n has 2^n elements and ℤ/p has p elements, we need p^n images to separate 2^n inputs under the linear map mod p, giving constraints on how the aᵢ distribute modulo small primes.

Step 4 (Antichain counting): The Boolean lattice {0,1}^n has maximum antichain of size C(n, ⌊n/2⌋) ~ 2^n/√n (Sperner). Since σ is order-preserving (all aᵢ > 0), elements of any antichain must map to distinct values, but their sums all lie near n·max(A)/2. This concentration + distinctness forces the range of σ to be at least ~2^n/√n, giving N ≥ a_n ≥ c·2^n/√n.

This yields N ≫ 2^n (up to polynomial factors). The full conjecture N ≥ 2^{n−1} requires sharper analysis of the lattice embedding.
